handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For microsoft-graph the manifest gained: MICROSOFT_GRAPH_BASE_URL. server.json gained: MICROSOFT_GRAPH_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: MICROSOFT_GRAPH_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: The novel-command seed store dates its security alert and its managed-device last-sync at now-1h instead of the literal 2099-01-01, so 'recent' keeps meaning recent, and the drift test now pins the absence of a stale reason
handfixes.why: This is the same class of TEST defect that PR #300 fixed in quickbooks, found by that PR's fleet-wide sweep of every YYYY-MM-DD literal under skills/*/cli/internal/**/*_test.go and reported-but-not-fixed there. The command under test reads the wall clock; the fixture pinned an absolute date. That pairing is only true until the calendar reaches the literal, at which point the assertion inverts and the test fails on the date rather than on a code change. Concretely: security triage computes since = time.Now().UTC() - window and drops alerts created before it (insights.SecurityTriage), and managed-devices drift computes staleBefore = time.Now().UTC() - days and appends a 'stale' reason to anything older (insights.DeviceDrift). Both fixtures used 2099-01-01 as a stand-in for 'recent', which only works while the calendar is short of it. Post-2099 the alert falls outside the 24h look-back and TestSecurityTriageCommand loses its only alert, and the device picks up a 'stale' reason it was never meant to have. The fix seeds both from a single clock read at now-1h: an hour is comfortably inside a 24h look-back and comfortably inside a 1-day freshness window, on any run date and in any time zone, since both the fixture and the command's cutoff are computed in UTC from the same clock. The device assertion was also made stronger rather than looser - it now asserts the device is NOT flagged stale, which keeps the seeded sync time load-bearing instead of decorative. Proven both directions by driving insights.SecurityTriage and insights.DeviceDrift directly: with a 48h-old createdDateTime (the post-2099 equivalent) totalOpen is 0 and the old assertion FAILS, and the drift reasons come back [noncompliant stale unencrypted] so the new no-stale assertion FAILS; with the now-1h fixtures totalOpen is 1 and the reasons are [noncompliant unencrypted], both PASSING.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the acceptance/novel test templates should never emit an absolute date literal whose truth depends on the calendar not having reached it. A fixture that means 'in the future' or 'recently' must be rendered as an offset from a single clock read, the way this fix does it. Same retro as the quickbooks novel-acceptance-fixtures-relative-to-today entry. File via /printing-press-retro.

A reprint that drops these edits fails these asserts and TestJournalCredentialHardening; restore them by hand (the fleet tool did not merge, owner rule 2026-10-28). handfixes.summary: sync and workflow archive (and the MCP sync and workflow_archive tools, which run them) read every resource's Graph collection to its end through the shared page walk (graphReadPages, graphReadSkipWindows for numberAssignments) before anything is stored or reported complete; a read that cannot be finished is a sync_error that stores nothing, and --max-pages still reports max_pages_cap_hit.
handfixes.why: Adversarial review 2026-11-06 (executed against the built binary, .review/adv-r3/t08.sh, t09.sh): Graph pages every collection with @odata.nextLink and may return fewer items than $top asks (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/paging). The generated sync paged every resource with $skip offsets, read no nextLink, and called a page shorter than $top the end, so GET /v1.0/security/alerts_v2?$top=100 answered with 50 alerts and a nextLink was one request, sync_complete total 50, warned 0, errored 0, exit 0, and security triage then showed 50 open alerts of 120; 6 users in pages of 2 stored 2; directory-roles and licenses (no pagination declared) and teams-users (no cursor) stopped at page 1 the same way. syncResource (generated sync.go) now reads each collection whole with syncGetGraphCollection (hand file msgraph_sync_pages.go) under sync's read policy: every page must carry a value array, every nextLink must name the configured host (one naming another host is an error and never followed) and a page not already read, a failed page fails the read, and the generated loop ends after that one read (complete, or max_pages_cap when --max-pages stopped it). A saved $skip cursor is not sent. The same change takes the first-response leniency off a walk that continues a collection (GetCollection's nextLink, a later $skip window), so a bare [] second page is an error, not the end. TestSyncReadsEveryPage, TestSyncIncompleteReadIsNeverComplete, TestSyncMaxPagesCapOnGraphPages and TestContinuationPageMustBeAGraphCollection fail on the old wiring; TestSyncBinaryReadsEveryPage drives the built CLI and MCP binaries. A reprint of sync.go restores the single-page read.
